gen-dafont-groovy-gf-puritan: Friendly and a bit funky, Groovy pinches its c almost shut and spaces its lowercase loosely. Puritan relaxes right beside it, rounded and plain sans, with oversized e and a counters that open wide to the side.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-questrial: Questrial reads flat and modern, almost stencil-cut, with a tall band of letters under short ascending stalks. And Groovy, with its nearly sealed c and loose spacing, adds the playful display voice on top.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada reads contemporary and full, its lowercase c, s and z standing tall with a clear opening at each curve. But Groovy sits above it, funky and nearly closed, so the sans underneath feels all the more open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big fills the line with a large x-height and terminals that finish well clear of the stem. Radio Canada Big gives Groovy's slit-like c and loose lowercase a sans partner that stays open where the heading squeezes shut.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-readex-pro: Friendly and funky, Groovy loosens its lowercase and pinches the c nearly closed, which is where it does its best work. Readex Pro does the opposite job, a plain sans with broad terminal gaps and a steady weight from word to word.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-roboto: Closed up, loose and cheerful. If Groovy were shrunk down, its unit-width strokes and slit-like c would crowd together, while Roboto stays easy with generous mouths on its round letters.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-ruda: Ruda reads clean and approachable, a sans-serif with a sizable x-height and wire-like strokes that open wide on the rounds. Groovy is best at pinching its c nearly shut for a funky headline; Ruda is best at staying open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-saira: Funky, pinched and loose, that is Groovy, its c almost sealed. Saira is the one to read, a plain sans whose s shows a gap you can see through and whose rounds stretch toward the top line.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch offers an approachable, contemporary plain sans with a clearly open mouth on the lowercase e and a compact gap up to the ascender line. Its best trait here is the contrast with Groovy, which keeps a plain unmodulated outline.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-savate: Round, clean and open, Savate gives every curved stroke an open jaw and a tall o that nearly matches the capital. And Groovy, friendly and funky with its almost-closed c, gives that sans something playful to sit under.
